headline: China sanctions ministers from two Taiwan allies

sources.title: China sanctions Paraguay and Belize officials over ties with Taiwan (AP, via CP24)
China sanctions 'pawn' Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties (Reuters, via Daily Maverick)
Taiwan allies Paraguay, Belize reject China sanctions on ministers (Taiwan News)
Paraguay and Belize condemn China sanctions (Taipei Times)
Taiwan hits back after China sanctions officials from Paraguay and Belize (video, TaiwanPlus News)

chunks.text: On October 12, 2026, China announced [[sanctions]] against two ministers from Paraguay and Belize. Beijing {{singled out}} Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister. The measures [[freeze]] any [[assets]] the two men hold in China. They also {{keep the ministers out}} of China, Hong Kong and Macau. The move came two days after Taiwan's [[national day]]. In a speech that day, Taiwan's president said the island would not {{give up}} its freedom.

verbs.correct: To choose certain people for punishment
verbs.wrong: To end someone's time in a job
verbs.why: Teachers often single out students who talk in class. Coaches sometimes single out one player for missing practice. China singled out a minister from Paraguay and a minister from Belize.

verbs.correct: To not let someone enter a place
verbs.wrong: To make someone pay a large fine
verbs.why: A tall fence keeps deer out of the garden. The new rules keep visitors out of the old building. The sanctions keep the two ministers out of China, Hong Kong and Macau.

verbs.correct: To agree to lose something important
verbs.wrong: To carry something in a parade
verbs.why: Some parents give up their jobs to help a sick child. Few people give up their right to vote easily. Taiwan's president said the island would not give up its freedom.

chunks.text: China sees Taiwan as part of its [[territory]]. Taiwan's government strongly rejects that view. The two sides have been ruled separately since a [[civil war]] in 1949. Paraguay and Belize are two of only 12 countries with [[formal ties]] with Taiwan. China has worked to {{win over}} these [[allies]]. In recent years, Nauru, Honduras and Nicaragua have {{cut off}} their ties with Taiwan. They now [[recognize]] the government in Beijing instead.

verbs.correct: To get someone to support you
verbs.wrong: To pay someone to stay quiet
verbs.why: A good mayor wins over voters with clear plans. A new boyfriend often wins over the family with good cooking. China has worked to win over the countries that have formal ties with Taiwan.

verbs.wrong: To send a new ambassador to a country
verbs.why: Some people cut off all contact with an old boss. Brothers sometimes cut off ties after a big fight. Nauru, Honduras and Nicaragua have cut off their ties with Taiwan.

chunks.text: China's foreign ministry said the sanctions protect the country's [[sovereignty]]. A [[spokesperson]] called the two ministers [[pawns]] of Taiwan's leaders. She said they had spread false claims about Chinese [[cyberattacks]]. In July, Paraguay said cyberattacks linked to China's government had affected its state computer systems. China denied the [[accusations]]. The spokesperson said Taiwan's allies could {{miss out on}} chances to grow. News agencies say the sanctions are mostly [[symbolic]], since such ministers rarely travel to China.

verbs.correct: To lose a chance to get something good
verbs.wrong: To owe a large amount of money
verbs.why: Late shoppers often miss out on the best deals. People who stay home miss out on free city concerts. China's spokesperson said Taiwan's allies could miss out on chances to grow.

chunks.text: Paraguay and Belize {{hit back}} at the sanctions. Paraguay's foreign ministry said they caused [[unnecessary friction]]. Paraguay's communications minister said his country would {{push ahead with}} its technology projects with Taiwan. He said Paraguay would even {{speed up}} the work. Belize said the measures would not change its [[foreign policy]]. It said it would {{stand by}} its minister. Taiwan's foreign ministry also {{spoke out}} against the sanctions. It said China had no right to [[interfere]] in Taiwan's ties with other countries.

verbs.correct: To answer an attack with strong words
verbs.wrong: To hold a meeting with neighbors
verbs.why: Famous singers often hit back at critics on social media. Politicians usually hit back at claims that they lied. Paraguay and Belize hit back at China's sanctions.

verbs.correct: To continue a plan despite problems
verbs.wrong: To share the cost of a plan
verbs.why: Some cities push ahead with new bridges despite protests. Many couples push ahead with their wedding even in the rain. Paraguay's minister said his country would push ahead with its technology projects with Taiwan.
Extra workers speed up the work on a big project. The new machine speeds up the whole process. The minister said Paraguay would speed up its work with Taiwan.

verbs.wrong: To give someone a new job
verbs.why: Good friends stand by each other in hard times. A loyal team stands by its coach after a loss. Belize said it would stand by its foreign minister.

verbs.correct: To say publicly that you disagree
verbs.wrong: To repeat what others have said
verbs.why: Students often speak out against unfair school rules. Some workers speak out against low pay at their company. Taiwan's foreign ministry spoke out against the sanctions.

mainIdea.s: China has punished two ministers from Paraguay and Belize because their countries keep formal ties with Taiwan. Both governments rejected the sanctions and will keep working with Taiwan.
mainIdea.why: China singled out the two ministers over their countries' ties with Taiwan. Paraguay and Belize hit back, and Paraguay will push ahead with its projects.

mainIdea.s: After Beijing placed sanctions on officials from two small countries in the Americas, both governments agreed to review their links with Taipei. Taiwan has asked both of them not to leave.
mainIdea.why: Close, but neither country agreed to review its ties. Paraguay said it would speed up its work with Taiwan, and Belize said it would stand by its minister.

mainIdea.s: Paraguay and Belize have signed a new trade deal with China that will lower prices on farm goods. Leaders from both countries traveled to Beijing to celebrate the agreement in October.
mainIdea.why: This story is about Chinese sanctions on two ministers. China singled them out because their countries have formal ties with Taiwan.

lines.text: Did you see that China {{singled out}} two ministers from Paraguay and Belize?
I did. What exactly did Beijing do to them?
It froze their assets in China. The sanctions also {{keep them out}} of China, Hong Kong and Macau.
Do they travel to China much?
Not really. News agencies say it's mostly symbolic, kind of [[a slap on the wrist]].
So why do it at all?
I think Beijing wants to [[send a message]] to Taiwan's other allies. It has worked to {{win over}} those countries for years.
And some of them did {{cut off}} their ties with Taiwan, right?
Yes, Nauru, Honduras and Nicaragua. Only 12 countries still have formal ties with Taiwan.
How did Paraguay and Belize react?
They both {{hit back}}. Paraguay's minister said they'll {{push ahead with}} their tech projects with Taiwan.
Sounds like he sees the sanctions as [[a badge of honor]].
Pretty much. He even wants to {{speed up}} the work.
Belize says it will {{stand by}} its foreign minister. Both countries plan to [[stand their ground]].
Its foreign ministry {{spoke out}} against the sanctions. China says Taiwan's allies could {{miss out on}} chances to grow.
When you look at [[the bigger picture]], this is really about China and Taiwan.

expressions.def: A very light punishment that does not cause much harm
ex: He only got a slap on the wrist for speeding.

expressions.def: Used to say that an action clearly shows others what you think or want
ex: The coach kept his best player on the bench to send a message to the team.

expressions.def: Something a person is proud of, even if others see it as bad
ex: For him, working two jobs is a badge of honor.
She sees her old running injuries as a badge of honor.

expressions.def: To refuse to change your position when others push you
ex: The workers stood their ground and kept their demands.
Even under pressure, the parents stood their ground.

expressions.def: The whole situation, not just one small part of it
ex: Try to see the bigger picture before you decide.
